steps.title: Implement the authorization URL, callback, and token exchange
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL with client_id, redirect_uri, and response_type=code. Exchange the returned code at /oauth2/token. Use PKCE (S256) if the client cannot keep a secret.
steps.doneWhen: The code builds the authorization URL, handles the callback, and exchanges the code for an access token in a test environment.

evidence.quote: Your Authorization URL should look like:

https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=MY_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=MY_REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code Wait for the end user to complete authorization on dropbox.com, whom is then redirected back to your URI with an authorization code in the
Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s client_secret to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls
Public clients should use the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256).

steps.title: Authorize one representative individual account
steps.detail: Sign in with a representative test account at dropbox.com, grant access through the authorization URL, and confirm the callback returns a code and an access token.
steps.doneWhen: The test account completes consent, the callback returns a code, and the token exchange returns an access token for that user.

evidence.quote: Overview When working with the Dropbox APIs, your app will access Dropbox on behalf of your users. You’ll need to have each user of your app sign into dropbox.com to

steps.title: List App Folder root with list_folder
steps.detail: Call list_folder with path set to an empty string to list the top level of the App Folder. Use the individual user's OAuth access token. Keep recursive false. Expected result: HTTP 200 with entries (names and metadata) plus a cursor and has_more flag. Do not call download, upload, move, or delete endpoints. Boundary check: send the same request with a nonexistent path such as /missing-folder-check; expect 409 and no entries. Continue pages with the retained list_folder/continue step until has_more is false.
steps.doneWhen: The first response is HTTP 200 with entries and a cursor that the retained list_folder/continue step accepts, and the nonexistent-path boundary check returns 409 without changing anything.
